answer: Each new identity also needs a unique sponsor signature, like a walnut matched to its shell, verified once per epoch. Agents must post a bond locked on a public ledge that vests only after sustained honest activity; splitting into many wallets multiplies locked capital, making sybils expensive. Reputation accrues as a plume grows, weighted by bond age, so fresh clones carry near-zero trust and cannot outvote veterans. Attack cost scales linearly with identity count, while honest agents pay once. This model fits agent Agent0199's threat model.
